title.narrative: Duurzame Oplossingen voor Syrische Vluchtelingen in Libanon

description.narrative: An “early majority” of policy makers and the broad public in Lebanon starts recognising the need for alternative approaches on the Syrian forced displacement crisis. They see the need for changes in legislation and policies and take measures to tackle problematic relationships with rightsholders and CSOs. An “early majority” of CSOs have strengthened their legitimacy, capacities, and influence on a rights-based durable solutions agenda, including the “triple nexus” and gender justice.

Our target groups are considered lobby targets (boundary partners), which are the groups with whom the programme interacts directly and in whom we anticipate opportunities to influence. These groups are: 1) national and international policymakers; 2) civil society and 3) the broad public. A detailled analysis of our target groups, and our intervention strategies towards them, can be found in 11.11.11’s Lebanon Theory of Change (provided as an annex).

The programme aims to contribute to the realisation of a rights-based “durable solutions” agenda for Syrian refugees in Lebanon. In order to ensure that refugees have access to such “durable solutions”, 11.11.11 and its local CSO partners will create a structural platform to operationalise the “triple nexus” between humanitarian, development and peacebuilding support.
Additionally, local CSO partners will be supported to increase their capacity to conduct innovative qualitative and quantitative research into various aspects of the Syrian refugee crisis in Lebanon, which will also serve as the basis for rights-based advocacy at national, regional and international level, and to counsel refugees on their mobility options. Particular attention will be paid to the protection situation of Syrian refugees, the gendered dynamics of forced displacement, and access to information on the conditions for a safe, voluntary, informed and dignified return.

description.narrative: R1: National and international political innovators in Lebanon promote systemic alternatives that favour a rights-based durable solutions agenda and gender justice, propose changes in legislation and policies, and take measures to tackle their problematic relationship with rightsholders and CSOs.

title.narrative: I 1.2: National and international political innovators change policies in favour of durable solutions

baseline.value: No indication that a group of political innovators are fully playing role to push for new legislation or policies, are working with other innovators, and work on innovative advocacy and movement building.

title.narrative: I 1.1: National and international political innovators promote alternative approaches in favour of durable solutions

baseline.value: No indication that a group of political innovators are fully playing their changemaker role.

description.narrative: R2: CSO innovators in Lebanon strengthen their legitimacy, capacities, and influence on policy debates on a rights-based durable solutions agenda, including discussions regarding the “triple nexus”. They ensure that donor interventions are better aligned with the needs of right-holders, and that rights-holders are in a better position to hold duty-bearers to account. CSOs contribute to policy change through joint projects, joint research and advocacy, and targeted awareness-raising efforts.

baseline.value: CSO early adaptors are present but not yet fully playing their role.
